dataset.source: UCI Machine Learning Repository – Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones (Anguita et al., 2013)
rows: Tri-axial accelerometer + gyroscope, smartphone on the waist
9 (body acc xyz, body gyro xyz, total acc xyz)

layers.name: Input window
layers.detail: 128 time steps × 9 inertial channels, standardised with training-set mean and standard deviation.

layers.name: Conv1D block 1
layers.detail: Conv1D(64 filters, kernel 5, same) → BatchNorm → ReLU → MaxPool(2) → Dropout(0.3). Each filter spans 0.1 s across all nine channels and learns a local motion primitive such as a foot strike.

layers.name: Conv1D block 2
layers.detail: Conv1D(128 filters, kernel 5, same) → BatchNorm → ReLU → MaxPool(2) → Dropout(0.3). Combines primitives into larger units such as a full step cycle, and shortens the sequence to 32 steps.

layers.name: LSTM 128 (sequence)
layers.detail: Reads the 32-step feature sequence and returns a hidden state at every step, modelling the order and rhythm of the learned primitives.

layers.name: LSTM 64 (final state)
layers.detail: A second recurrent layer that compresses the whole window into a single 64-dimensional summary vector.

layers.name: Dense 64 + ReLU
layers.detail: Fully connected layer with dropout that re-mixes the temporal summary before classification.

layers.name: Softmax output
layers.detail: Six probabilities, one per activity. The largest is the prediction.

training: monitor val_loss, patience 8, restore best weights
15% of the training set, stratified by class

improvements.how: Add a parallel input carrying the low-frequency gravity component or tilt angles and concatenate it with the LSTM output before the classifier.
Replace the final LSTM summary with attention pooling over the 32 LSTM outputs; the weights become an interpretable heat-map.
Gaussian jitter, magnitude scaling, small 3-D rotations (different phone orientations) and time-warping (different walking speeds).
KerasTuner or Optuna over kernel size, filters, LSTM units, dropout and learning rate, using validation folds grouped by subject.
Put more weight on the sitting/standing boundary; add label smoothing and cosine learning-rate decay.
Average several seeds or architectures (CNN-LSTM, CNN-GRU, Bi-LSTM); majority-vote or HMM over consecutive windows.
Group k-fold by subject so results reflect variation across people and include confidence intervals.
Fine-tune only the classifier head on a short calibration recording (transfer learning).
At about 230k parameters (under 1 MB) the model already fits a phone or Raspberry Pi; post-training quantisation shrinks it further.

futureWork: Implement the orientation-feature branch and attention pooling, and measure the effect on sitting/standing F1.
Adopt leave-subjects-out cross-validation and an ablation study (CNN-only, LSTM-only, CNN-LSTM, Bi-LSTM, CNN-GRU).
Explore Transformer-style self-attention and Temporal Convolutional Networks as alternatives to the LSTM.
Extend to richer datasets (WISDM, PAMAP2, Opportunity) with transfer learning between them.
Deploy the quantised model on a smartphone or Raspberry Pi for real-time recognition.
Add personalisation through few-shot fine-tuning and investigate privacy-preserving federated training.
